citation: Greenleaf, C. L., Litman, C., Hanson, T. L., Rosen, R., Boscardin, C. K., Herman, J., Schneider, S. A., Madden, S., & Jones, B. (2011). Integrating Literacy and Science in Biology: Teaching and Learning Impacts of Reading Apprenticeship Professional Development. American Educational Research Journal, 48(3), 647-717. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831210384839
report_number: AERJ 48(3):647-717 (DOI 10.3102/0002831210384839). Effect sizes extracted from the openly published NSF ROLE funder final report: Greenleaf, Hanson, Herman, Litman, Madden, Rosen, Boscardin, Schneider & Silver (2009), 'Integrating Literacy and Science Instruction in High School Biology: Impact on Teacher Practice, Student Engagement, and Student Achievement', Final report to the National Science Foundation, NSF Grant #0440379 (ROLE program), WestEd & UCLA/CRESST.
design: Group(school)-randomized controlled trial (cluster RCT, assignment = school). California high schools serving high proportions of underrepresented/EL students were pair-matched on the 2004 School Characteristics Index, then randomly assigned within pair to treatment vs wait-listed business-as-usual control. From 105 recruited teachers in 83 schools, ~87 teachers in 70 pair-matched high schools participated in Year 1 (target >=25 schools per arm). Intervention = ~10 days of Reading Apprenticeship professional development for high-school biology teachers (metacognitive reading-comprehension routines integrated into biology instruction) delivered across two summers + school year; comparison = business-as-usual (no alternative PD). Outcomes = California Standards Tests (CST) in English Language Arts, Reading Comprehension, and Biology; students grades 9-10 biology (registry grade band 7-12). Impacts estimated with two-level hierarchical (multilevel) regression accounting for clustering by school, including randomization-strata (pair) and student/teacher covariates; pretest adjustment present in the longitudinal models (individual prior ELA/Math CST) and via teacher-aggregated 2004/05 prior scores in the cross-sectional models. End-of-treatment wave = 2006/07 (end of Year 2). Two analytic test-score samples: (a) cross-sectional, anonymous unlinked, more representative (max 5,436 students in 49 schools) -- the report's headline result, matching the AERJ abstract; (b) longitudinal, parental-consent linked subsample with individual pretests (max 1,236 students in 45 schools).
problems: SOURCE NOTE (legal OA): the cited publication is the SAGE/AERJ journal article (DOI 10.3102/0002831210384839), which Unpaywall/OpenAlex report as CLOSED (no legal OA copy of the journal version). I did NOT extract from any paywalled or pirated copy. Instead I extracted the identical RCT effect sizes from the openly published NSF ROLE funder final report (WestEd/UCLA-CRESST, NSF Grant #0440379) at www2.wested.org -- same authors, same trial, and the report's headline cross-sectional effect sizes (ELA 0.23, Reading Comprehension 0.24, Biology 0.28) exactly match the figures quoted for this study (Greenleaf et al. 2011). This is a funder repository copy, permitted by the spec. KEY AMBIGUITIES: (1) Table 11 reports two same-timepoint (2006/07, end of Year 2) samples -- a CROSS-SECTIONAL sample (n<=5,436 in 49 schools; the report's headline, statistically significant) and a LONGITUDINAL sample (n<=1,236 in 45 schools; pretest-adjusted at the student level, all null). I extracted all six contrasts; outcome_role=primary is assigned to the cross-sectional Reading-Comprehension and Biology rows (the report's confirmatory/headline outcomes); the longitudinal rows are the same-timepoint alternative-sample estimates and are labelled is_full_sample=true but flagged. The meta-analysis very likely used the cross-sectional headline figures (0.23/0.24/0.28). (2) The report gives the standardized effect as Diff/SD = difference / pooled SD of the outcome (a covariate-adjusted SMD) but does NOT publish impact SEs, design-effect ICCs, n_clusters per outcome, or per-arm n's. I therefore took Diff/SD directly as d and applied Hedges' J (large df, J~1.0). I derived g_se from the reported two-sided p-value and the standardized point estimate (se_d = |d| / z, z = inverse-normal(1 - p/2)); because these p-values come from the multilevel (school-clustered) models, the resulting SEs are already cluster-adjusted, so cluster_adjusted=true and n_clusters is set to the schools in each sample. ICC is null (NOT reported; not guessed). (3) Per-arm n_t/n_c are null -- only total analytic n and school counts are given. (4) ELA, Reading Comprehension, and Biology CST are independent state standardized tests (standardized_independent). Teacher-practice, OTL-engagement, and Integrated Learning Assessment outcomes were skipped (not state-test student achievement). (5) Selective (differential) teacher attrition is noted by the authors -- impacts only reached significance after covariate adjustment; treat the longitudinal-sample nulls and the cross-sectional positives with this caveat. (6) df for J uses student-level total n (conservative; true effective df is lower under clustering, but J is essentially 1 at these n's so the choice is immaterial).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Reading Apprenticeship PD for high-school biology teachers vs business-as-usual control -- cross-sectional analytic sample (report's headline, 2006/07)
effect_sizes.test_name: California Standards Test (CST) Biology scale score, 2006/07
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's Diff/SD = covariate-adjusted difference / pooled SD = 0.28 taken as d (Biology CST scale-score difference 13.61 / pooled SD); g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df ~= 5434 (J = 0.99986) so g = 0.2800. g_se derived from the reported two-sided p = .01 and point estimate: z = invnorm(1 - p/2) = 2.576, se_d = |d|/z = 0.28/2.576 = 0.1087, g_se = J*se_d = 0.1087; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.01181. From the school-clustered multilevel model so cluster_adjusted = true.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.34 Table 11 (cross-sectional Biology CST row); discussion p.33
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory science outcome; statistically significant (p=.01). Treatment mean 336.52 vs control 322.91 (Biology CST scale score). Cross-sectional sample = anonymous/unlinked, more representative (max 5,436 students in 49 schools); covariates = randomization strata, race/ethnicity, EL status, gender, plus 2004/05 teacher-aggregated prior biology & reading-comprehension scores (teacher-level pretest, not individual). Independent state standardized test. Authors note selective control-teacher attrition; impacts significant only after covariate adjustment.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Reading Apprenticeship PD for high-school biology teachers vs business-as-usual control -- cross-sectional analytic sample (report's headline, 2006/07)
effect_sizes.g_method: Outcome is z-standardized (mean 0, SD 1 across the analytic sample), so the reported difference 0.24 IS the standardized effect d (= Diff/SD = 0.24). g = J*d, df ~= 5434, J = 0.99986, g = 0.2400. g_se from reported two-sided p = .02: z = 2.326, se_d = 0.24/2.326 = 0.1032, g_se = J*se_d = 0.1032; g_var = 0.01064. School-clustered multilevel model -> cluster_adjusted = true.

Independent state standardized test.
